summary: Gives Best Current Practice guidelines for operating DNS where queries and responses travel over a mix of IPv4 and IPv6 networks. It was later replaced by RFC 10001.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3901 gives operational rules to keep DNS names reachable while queries and referrals use a mix of IPv4 and IPv6. It recommends that each zone have an IPv4-reachable authoritative server and that recursive servers be IPv4-only or dual-stack; RFC 10001 later updated this memo.

subtitle: Operational guidelines for DNS queries over mixed IPv4 and IPv6 networks.

tldr.problem: During the transition to mixed IPv4 and IPv6 transport, DNS referrals could lead a resolver to a name server reachable only over an IP version it cannot use.
tldr.mechanism: The memo recommends IPv4-only or dual-stack recursive name servers and at least one IPv4-reachable authoritative name server for every zone.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3901 is a Best Current Practice updated by RFC 10001.

facts.label: Authoritative zone policy
facts.value: At least one IPv4-reachable name server

today: RFC 3901 is a Best Current Practice updated by RFC 10001.

sections.title: Avoiding DNS Name-Space Fragmentation
sections.content:
A resolver follows referrals from the root toward the name server authoritative for a requested name. If a server in the chain is reachable only over IPv4 or IPv6 that the resolver cannot use, the resolver cannot finish the lookup.

During a transition with DNS data available over IPv4, IPv6, or both, zones reachable only over IPv6 could fragment the name space available to IPv4-only hosts. The memo focuses on preserving the existing IPv4-reachable name space.
sections.plainLanguage: A DNS lookup follows directions from one server to another. If a referral points to a server the resolver cannot reach over its available IP version, the lookup stops.

sections.title: Recommended Operating Policies
sections.content:
Every recursive name server should be either IPv4-only or dual-stack; the memo rules out IPv6-only recursive servers. An IPv6-only server can forward queries to a dual-stack recursive server.

Every DNS zone should have at least one IPv4-reachable authoritative name server. Zone validation should also ensure that a child delegation has at least one IPv4 address record available for its name servers.
sections.plainLanguage: A recursive server should handle IPv4 or both IPv4 and IPv6. Each zone should also have an authoritative server reachable over IPv4 so IPv4-only resolvers can follow referrals.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: The memo says these guidelines introduce no new security considerations into DNS or associated operational scenarios. RFC 3901 is a Best Current Practice and is updated by RFC 10001.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo says its operating guidelines add no new DNS security considerations. RFC 10001 later updated it.
